format.chart: 32-team double-elimination bracket with reseeding at every stage (Joe, 2026-10-23). Winners bracket stages of 16/8/4/2/1 series counting the opening round; losers bracket stages of 8/8/4/4/2/2/1/1, alternating survivor-only and drop-in rounds; grand final plus one reset series if the one-loss finalist wins the first final. 62 series total, 63 with the reset. At every stage the pool is reseeded by original tournament seed and paired highest vs lowest, second-highest vs second-lowest, so the top seed always draws the lowest-seeded survivor. See BRACKET.md.
format.home_pattern: 2-2-1-1-1, higher seed home first (Joe, 2026-10-23): Games 1-2 higher seed, 3-4 lower seed, 5 higher seed, 6 lower seed, 7 higher seed.
format.formation_gate: A stage forms only when every series feeding it is complete: Winners Round 2 and Losers Round 1 form when all 16 opening series finish; each later stage forms when its feeding stage finishes (plus the corresponding winners stage for losers drop-in stages). No pairing exists before its stage forms (Joe's reseeding rule, 2026-10-23).
format.final: Winners-bracket champion (undefeated) vs losers-bracket champion (one loss), best of 7; if the one-loss team wins, one reset series decides the championship.

stat_keying: Player stats are stored per (team, player_id). A player rostered by two teams has one line per team, never merged.

series.label: Opening Round, Series 3
series.provenance: Played in Payoff Pitch as tournament series R1-03 on 2026-10-24 (FAC deck mode, version 2 pitcher cards, the pitcher addendum, manager traits for both clubs: Francona for Boston, Cash for Tampa Bay in tournament mode with the Opener refused under Joe's ruling that relievers do not start tournament games; the fatigue fix layer in both games) under Joe's ruling that the tournament is a Payoff Pitch tournament and APBA is closed. Games 1-2 are recorded here from the series' saved state files (payoff-pitch-rays/state_series_bos_tb_g1..g2.json) by record_r1_03_pp.py, following the R1-02 script's mechanism; the series is in progress, Boston leading 2-0, and later games append the same way. Tampa Bay plays in the host engine's 'PHA' guest slot, so the state files key the Rays as 'PHA'; those keys map to TB in the records. Field mapping: rolls holds the FAC flip history (card number and draw purpose), the Payoff Pitch equivalent of the dice record; final_grades is empty because Payoff Pitch has no letter grades, and pitcher fatigue end states are in fatigue_end_states, from the fix layer stored in both states; resolutions and n41 are null because those APBA counters do not exist in Payoff Pitch; batting sac is the states' single SH category, with sf and ibb null because the states do not split them; pitching lines carry hr allowed, which the states record, and hb null, which they do not record by pitcher. Availability ran under the house outs convention: caps_in and caps_out carry it in the archive's encoding (player_id: max outs next game, 0 would mean unavailable). Games 3-7 were added from Joe's official box scores on 2026-10-25. Those box scores carry the linescore, batting, pitching, decisions, and the short recap. They do not carry the FAC roll log, so games/R1-03-G3.json through G7.json store an empty rolls array. Games 3-7 have no per-game calendar date in the box scores; the date is null. The series summary dates the series to 2026-10-24 and 2026-10-25. Games 1-2 stay dated 2026-10-24. Boston won the series 4-3 and advances on the winners side at 1-0. Tampa Bay drops to the losers side at 0-1 and is not eliminated.

carry.rotation_note: Series complete, Boston 4-3. Starters in the box scores: Boston Martinez, Clemens, Young, Wood, Grove, Martinez, Clemens; Tampa Bay Price, Shields, Snell, McClanahan, Kazmir, Price, Shields.

narratives.text: In Game 1, Pedro Martinez threw a no-hitter, nine innings, no hits, two walks, eleven strikeouts, and Jimmie Foxx homered twice in a 6-0 win.

In Game 2, Roger Clemens struck out fourteen over 7.1 innings; Toby Hall's sixth-inning homer gave Tampa Bay its first lead of the series, and Boston answered with three runs in the bottom of the inning against a fatigued James Shields, Jonathan Papelbon closing the 3-1 win.

In Game 3, Blake Snell threw a complete-game shutout, three hits and eight strikeouts, and the only run scored in the bottom of the ninth: Carl Crawford doubled off Cy Young and Joey Wendle doubled him home off Papelbon.

In Game 4, all six Tampa Bay runs were charged to Smoky Joe Wood, on Jason Bartlett's three-run homer in the fourth and Carlos Pena's three-run homer in the seventh; Shane McClanahan won 6-3 at 8.2 innings, and Foxx homered twice in the loss.

Game 5 was the turn of the series. Tampa Bay led 5-0 into the seventh at Fenway. Nomar Garciaparra's homer got Boston started, and the ninth produced four runs: Scott Kazmir left with a three-run lead, no outs and runners on first and third, both inherited runners scored, and Ted Williams tied the game with a single off Pete Fairbanks. Papelbon, in since the eighth, held Tampa Bay through the tenth while fatigued, and Foxx led off the bottom of the tenth with the walk-off homer, 6-5.

Tampa Bay leveled it a second time in Game 6, and did it against Martinez at his best: he threw a complete game, four hits and eleven strikeouts, and lost 3-1 because every run in the game scored in the third inning. Boston's run came home on a double play; Bartlett tripled, Hall singled him in, and Wendle hit a two-run homer. David Price walked nobody in eight innings and Fairbanks saved it.

Game 7 belonged to Clemens. He went 8.2 innings, five hits, one earned run, one walk, sixteen strikeouts, and was never fatigued. Tampa Bay's only run was Evan Longoria's fourth-inning homer. Shields broke in the fifth, when two Boston runs scored on bases-loaded walks against his fatigued reads, and Boston ran the score to 8-1. Papelbon recorded the final out.

series.label: Opening Round, Series 4
series.provenance: Played in Payoff Pitch as tournament series R1-04 on 2026-10-25 (FAC deck mode, version 2 pitcher cards, the pitcher addendum, the fatigue fix layer, and manager traits governing both clubs: Sparky Anderson for Detroit, Bob Brenly for Arizona, with the official bunt-grade overlay live for Brenly's Small Ball) under Joe's ruling that the tournament is a Payoff Pitch tournament and APBA is closed. Detroit home games (1, 2, 5) were played on the 1986 Tiger Stadium park card under Joe's ruling; Arizona home games (3, 4, 6) on the standard league-average composite park Joe accepted; the printed Chase Field card from the publisher's 2024 set was verified into the managers' reference folder but never adopted. The series is recorded here from the series' saved state files (payoff-pitch-diamondbacks/state_series_det_ari_g1..g6.json) by record_r1_04_pp.py, following the R1-03 scripts' mechanism, and it is COMPLETE: Detroit wins 4-2. Game 5 was played twice on 2026-10-25: the first playing (Arizona 8, Detroit 5, seed 20261212) was set aside by Joe's ruling after he had the game played fresh from scratch, and the fresh re-play (Detroit 3, Arizona 1, seed 20261220) stands as the official Game 5 recorded here; the superseded playing is preserved in the series home (PP_R1_04_G5_SUPERSEDED.md and its state files) and recorded nowhere in this archive. Detroit played Games 3-6 under Joe's lineup ruling: Harry Heilmann started in left field in Bobby Veach's batting slot, priced straight across on his carded right-field line, and Veach never appeared in the series after Game 2. Game 1 was stopped in the first inning at an unanswerable rare-play branch and resumed under Joe's count-based carry ruling (the lingering-effects wrapper extended with count-based TOUGH and IN-PLAY flags). Arizona plays in the host engine's 'OPP' guest slot, so the state files key the Diamondbacks as 'OPP'; those keys map to ARI in the records. Field mapping: rolls holds the FAC flip history (card number and draw purpose), the Payoff Pitch equivalent of the dice record; final_grades is empty because Payoff Pitch has no letter grades, and pitcher fatigue end states are in fatigue_end_states, from the fix layer stored in every state, except the two 0-BF phantom changes (Andrew Chafin in Game 2, Dizzy Trout in Game 4, each a driver-recorded change after the final out, disclosed in those game records), who faced no batter, carry no fatigue record in their states, and are recorded unfatigued; resolutions and n41 are null because those APBA counters do not exist in Payoff Pitch; batting sac is the states' single SH category, with sf and ibb null because the states do not split them; pitching lines carry hr allowed, which the states record, and hb null, which they do not record by pitcher. Availability ran under the house outs convention: caps_in and caps_out carry it in the archive's encoding (player_id: max outs next game, 0 means unavailable). Detroit advances on the winners side at 1-0 in series; Arizona drops to the losers side at 0-1 and is not eliminated. No later-round shell fills from this series alone: Winners Round 2 and Losers Round 1 form only when all 16 opening series are complete (the formation gate), and advance_bracket was run at completion and changed nothing outside this series.

carry.rotation_note: Series complete, Detroit 4-2. Starters in the box scores: Detroit Newhouser, Verlander, Lolich, Bridges, Morris, Newhouser; Arizona Johnson, Schilling, Webb, Gallen, Kelly, Johnson.

narratives.text: In Game 1, Randy Johnson threw eight scoreless innings of four-hit ball at Tiger Stadium; Arizona's runs came on singles off Hal Newhouser in the fourth and fifth, and the closer rule lifted Johnson at 24 outs with the two-run lead, Jose Valverde finishing the 2-0 shutout.

In Game 2, Arizona won 7-5 in thirteen innings. Detroit's three-run sixth, on Hank Greenberg's two-run triple, took a 4-3 lead; Corbin Carroll tied it with a seventh-inning homer, Gabriel Moreno's tenth-inning squeeze put Arizona ahead, Charlie Gehringer answered with a leadoff homer, and Ketel Marte's two-run homer in the thirteenth won it, Byung-Hyun Kim getting George Kell with the bases loaded for the save after Valverde was ejected for hitting Bill Freehan a second time.

In Game 3, Detroit's first inning decided it: Ty Cobb singled and stole second, Gehringer tripled him home and Al Kaline singled in a second run, and Mickey Lolich allowed three hits in seven innings in a 4-1 win. Harry Heilmann, starting in left field under Joe's lineup ruling, doubled and scored in the seventh. Freehan was ejected in the first inning, before he batted, for arguing a rare-play call.

In Game 4, Tommy Bridges threw a three-hitter with thirteen strikeouts and no Arizona runner reached third; Zac Gallen pitched a complete game and lost 3-0 on two earned runs. Willie Hernandez, capped at three outs by the rest rule, had to be lifted in the ninth in a save situation, and Denny McLain recorded the save.

Game 5 was played twice, and only the second playing counts. Jack Morris was scoreless into the eighth and Merrill Kelly threw a complete-game one-hitter and lost: George Kell's two-run triple was Detroit's only hit, and the third run scored hitless in the seventh on two Arizona errors and a squeeze. Hernandez saved the 3-1 win. The first playing, an 8-5 Arizona win, was set aside by Joe's ruling and is not in this archive.

Game 6 was played twice, and only the second playing counts. In the replay, played in the app on 2026-11-09 under Joe's adoption ruling, Detroit ended the series in Arizona in a rout: Freehan's three-run homer in the second and Veach's three-run homer in the third knocked Johnson out, Kaline homered in the seventh, and Freehan's second homer, a two-run shot in the ninth, finished a four-hit, seven-RBI game. Newhouser threw a three-hit complete game in the 13-4 win. The original Game 6, Detroit's 10-3 win on Heilmann's three-run homer, is preserved in the Diamondbacks records at archive/replaced/.

series.label: Opening Round, Series 5
series.provenance: Played in Payoff Pitch as tournament series R1-05 on 2026-10-26 (FAC deck mode, version 2 pitcher cards, the pitcher addendum live for both clubs, the fatigue fix layer, the official bunt-grade overlay at the bunt seam, the universal DH, manager traits for both clubs: La Russa for St. Louis, Black for Colorado) under Joe's ruling that the tournament is a Payoff Pitch tournament and APBA is closed. Game 1 was played twice. The first playing (2026-10-26, St. Louis 10, Colorado 8, seed 20261301) was set aside by Joe's ruling of 2026-10-27 after he had the game played fresh as a co-managed human audit, and the fresh playing (2026-10-27, St. Louis 7, Colorado 2, seed 20261311, Bob Gibson a complete-game win, Ubaldo Jimenez the loss, no save, no substitution and no rare play) stands as the official Game 1 recorded here, built from the adopted state file (payoff-pitch-rockies/state_series_stl_col_g1.json, a byte copy of the candidate state state_series_stl_col_g1_comanaged_candidate_seed20261311.json) by record_r1_05_g1_replacement_pp.py with the same field mapping as the original recording; the superseded playing is preserved in the series home (archive/replaced/PP_R1_05_G1_seed20261301.md and its state file) and recorded nowhere in this archive. The series is complete, St. Louis winning 4-0, and Games 2 to 4 append the same way the original recording described. Colorado plays in the host engine's 'OPP' guest slot, so the state file keys the Rockies as 'OPP'; those keys map to COL in the records. Field mapping: rolls holds the FAC flip history (card number and draw purpose), the Payoff Pitch equivalent of the dice record; final_grades is empty because Payoff Pitch has no letter grades, and pitcher fatigue end states are in fatigue_end_states, from the fix layer stored in the state; resolutions and n41 are null because those APBA counters do not exist in Payoff Pitch; batting sac is the state's single SH category, with sf and ibb null because the states do not split them; pitching lines carry hr allowed, which the states record, and hb null, which they do not record by pitcher. The adopted Game 1 contained no rare play and no substitution: no plate appearance carried an initial percentile 00, and Ozzie Smith played the whole game at shortstop. No save arose: Gibson finished the game himself, and Joe's closer branch never fired because the 9th-inning lead was 5, outside its 1-to-3 band. Availability out of the adopted Game 1 ran under the house outs convention: caps_in and caps_out carry it in the archive's encoding (player_id: max outs next game, 0 meaning unavailable, a number meaning capped at that many outs); Gibson (27 outs, a complete game) and Jimenez (17 outs) are unavailable for the next game under the fatigue layer's rows, and Boone Logan (7 relief outs) is capped at 3 outs, which caps_out carries. CASCADE NOTE: Games 2 to 4 were played on 2026-10-26 under the superseded Game 1's availability and bench-watch flags (Jason Isringhausen sat out Game 2 under the superseded game's bar and Boone Logan pitched Game 2 without this game's cap, and the bench review behind the Games 3 and 4 lineup changes was run off the superseded game's lines); by Joe's adoption ruling those games stand exactly as played and as recorded, and their records are not rewritten. Game 2 was recorded the same way by record_r1_05_g2_pp.py from state_series_stl_col_g2.json (seed 20261302, played 2026-10-26): St. Louis 8, Colorado 3, St. Louis leading 2-0. Game 2 contained one hand-resolved rare play: the Bases Empty IN-PLAY 80-84 storm entry in the bottom of the 6th (flip 83; the delay roll came up 2d6 = 8, an 80-minute delay), under which both pitchers stiffened and were replaced (Boone Logan by Matt Belisle at once, Dizzy Dean by Al Brazle for the top of the 7th) and Ken Boyer's interrupted at-bat was re-resolved on his IN-PLAY section against Belisle. Al Brazle earns the save (three-run entry state at 5-2, bases empty, and three full innings to finish; the three-inning prong independently, per the R1-04 Game 6 precedent). Jason Isringhausen was unavailable for Game 2 under Game 1's caps_out and did not appear; Al Brazle is unavailable for Game 3 under Game 2's caps_out. Game 3 was recorded the same way by record_r1_05_g3_pp.py from state_series_stl_col_g3.json (seed 20261303, played 2026-10-26): St. Louis 1, Colorado 0, at Coors Field on its real printed 2024 card, St. Louis leading 3-0. The game was hosted on the series' host engine (St. Louis's v2 engine) with the venue carried by in-process re-pointings: the park slot held the printed Coors card, the engine's halves were re-pointed so Colorado batted last as the home club in its guest slot, and init_spans was re-pointed to stamp each starter's span with the half his club actually bats in; the host engine's BALLPARK log text still says Busch Stadium, a borrowed label only. Joe's lineup rulings for Game 3 (his post-game bench review rule) are inside the record: Lou Brock started in LF in Jim Edmonds's 5th slot and Joe Medwick played CF in his own 6th slot, off his card (carded LF only, his defense priced on his carded line), for St. Louis, and Yorvit Torrealba caught in Elias Diaz's 8th slot for Colorado; Edmonds and Diaz never appeared and neither club made a substitution of any kind. The game contained no rare play. Adam Wainwright threw eight shutout innings and Aaron Cook a complete game in the loss; the only run scored in the top of the 7th (Brock walked, stole 2nd, and scored on Medwick's single). Joe's closer branch fired for the first time in the series, summoning Ryan Helsley for the bottom of the 9th (lead of one, starter at 24 outs); Helsley earns the save on every prong. Al Brazle was unavailable for Game 3 under Game 2's caps_out and did not appear; his bar covered Game 3 only. Game 3 produced no caps: its only reliever, Helsley, recorded 3 outs. Game 4 was recorded the same way by record_r1_05_g4_pp.py from state_series_stl_col_g4.json (seed 20261304, played 2026-10-26): St. Louis 10, Colorado 7, at Coors Field on its printed 2024 card, and St. Louis wins the series 4-0. Joe's Game 4 lineup ruling (his post-game bench review rule) is inside the record: Ellis Burks started at leadoff in CF in Charlie Blackmon's slot (Blackmon benched, never appeared), Yorvit Torrealba stayed at catcher (Elias Diaz never appeared), and St. Louis fielded its Game 3 nine unchanged (Brock in LF, Medwick in CF off his card); neither club made a substitution of any kind. The game contained no rare play. Game 4 was an elimination game for Colorado, so the house hard rule's starter-in-relief exception stood open for Colorado all game; it was never used (Colorado's pitchers were its starter German Marquez and the pen arms Boone Logan and Rafael Betancourt). Harry Brecheen earned the win (7.1 innings; St. Louis led wire to wire); German Marquez took the loss, lifted book-fatigued in the 5th. Ryan Helsley finished the 9th with no save: he entered with one out, the bases empty and a three-run lead, so the tying run was not on base, at bat or on deck at his entry, and his two outs are short of the one-inning prong, the same standard applied to his Game 1 finish. Errors: Joe Medwick (CF) and Harry Brecheen (P), one each, both 2-base errors on DEFENSE reads; Colorado was errorless. Game 4 produced caps for Logan and Betancourt (7 relief outs each, capped at 3), of record only: the series is complete, St. Louis advances on the winners side at 1-0 in series and Colorado drops to the losers side at 0-1, not eliminated; advance_bracket was run at completion and filled no shell (5 of 16 opening series complete).

carry.rotation_note: The series ended in four games. Each club used the first four starters of its posted order (STL: Gibson, Dean, Wainwright, Brecheen; COL: Jimenez, Freeland, Cook, Marquez), so the cycle carries to the fifth man in each club's next series (Carpenter for St. Louis, Chacin for Colorado). Full posted orders: STL Gibson, Dean, Wainwright, Brecheen, Carpenter; COL Jimenez, Freeland, Cook, Marquez, Chacin.
carry.arms: Bullpen availability resets between rounds; no pitcher carries a restriction out of this series. Availability inside the series ran under the house outs convention: Jason Isringhausen was unavailable in Game 2 after 9 outs in Game 1; Al Brazle was unavailable in Game 3 after 9 outs in Game 2, his bar covering Game 3 only. Game 4 produced caps that stand of record only (Boone Logan and Rafael Betancourt, 7 relief outs each, capped at 3 outs); Bruce Sutter (3 outs) and Ryan Helsley (2 outs) were uncapped.

games.game_recap: Winners Round 2, Series 2, Game 3 at Kansas City (Kauffman Stadium). Booked from the app export, played by Joe in the app: the Gazette scorecard PDF, the scorecard photo, the graded manager-decision log, the box score CSV (with its PLAYS (JSON) section) and the standalone plays JSON. San Francisco's 18-hit attack buried Kansas City early. Willie Mays doubled to open the game and Will Clark followed with a two-run home run. Three more scored in the 2nd: Mays's two-run double on John McGraw's hit and run (graded +2.37) scored Buster Posey and Art Fletcher, and Mel Ott singled Mays home. Jeff Kent's double in the 3rd scored Willie McCovey to make it 6-0. Mark Gubicza takes the loss, charged with all six runs (9 hits and the Clark home run in 15 batters faced; McCovey and Kent both reached and scored off him to open the 3rd before Joakim Soria entered). Juan Marichal takes the win: eight innings, seven hits, no walks, eight strikeouts, and all five Kansas City runs charged to him, every one on a home run: Salvador Pérez's two-run shot in the 2nd after Alex Gordon's double, back-to-back solo homers by Danny Tartabull and Gordon in the 4th, and Tartabull's second solo homer in the 6th. Decisions: no source prints them (the Gazette carries no win/loss/save annotations and the export prints no decisions section), so they are derived from the play log and the run charges. There is no save: Robb Nen pitched a scoreless 9th with a five-run lead, walking John Mayberry (who took second on Nen's wild pitch) and striking out Darrell Porter to end it. San Francisco added one run in the 7th off Dan Quisenberry: Barry Bonds singled and was caught stealing (Pérez to Witt), McCovey doubled, Frankie Frisch pinch-ran for him and scored on Posey's single after Kent's single moved him to third. Three more scored in the 9th off David Cone, McGraw's second hit and run producing Bonds's two-run home run (+2.39, the best grade of the game), Frisch then tripling and scoring on Kent's single. San Francisco books ten RBI for ten runs (Mays 2, Clark 2, Bonds 2, Kent 2, Ott 1, Posey 1). Kansas City used eight pitchers: Gubicza and seven relievers at exactly one inning each (Soria, Herrera, Mingori, Holland, Quisenberry, Cone, Montgomery). The game was errorless. Fielding from the box score's printed fielding section: San Francisco 27 putouts and 7 assists with no double plays; Kansas City 27 putouts and 11 assists with two double plays, both 6-4-3 on Matt Williams grounders (the 7th, Witt to White to Mayberry; the 9th, Witt unassisted at second to Mayberry), and Williams is printed with 2 GIDP. Wild pitches: Soria 1 for Kansas City (the 3rd) and Nen 1 for San Francisco (the 9th); no passed balls. Bob Brenly, McGraw's bottom-of-the-8th defensive replacement at catcher for Posey, walked in his only plate appearance in the 9th and caught the last two innings. Frisch stayed in McCovey's DH slot and batted once, the 9th-inning triple. Manager grades: Yost graded 10 decisions (7 paid off, 3 backfired): six of his seven pitching changes paid off (Soria +0.85, Herrera +0.73, Mingori +0.73, Holland +0.73, Cone +0.73, Montgomery +0.61) and only the Quisenberry change backfired (-0.77); the Mayberry pinch hit paid off (+0.50), the Porter pinch hit backfired (-0.73), and his bottom-of-the-1st hit and run backfired (-0.76). McGraw graded 7 (4 paid off, 1 backfired, 2 neutral): both hit and runs paid off (+2.37 and +2.39, the two best grades of the game), the Frisch pinch run paid off (+0.59) and the Brenly substitution paid off (+0.48); the top-of-the-9th steal send backfired (-0.86, Kent held), the top-of-the-7th steal was neutral (-0.11, Bonds caught stealing) and the Nen change was neutral (+0.23). Counting checks: San Francisco plate appearances 45 equal Kansas City batters faced (Gubicza 15, Soria 4, Herrera 4, Mingori 4, Holland 3, Quisenberry 5, Cone 7, Montgomery 3); Kansas City plate appearances 35 equal San Francisco batters faced (Marichal 31, Nen 4). games.game_recap: Winners Round 2, Series 2, Game 4 at Kansas City (Kauffman Stadium). Booked from the app export, played by Joe in the app: the Gazette scorecard PDF, the scorecard photo, the graded manager-decision log, the box score CSV (with its PLAYS (JSON) section) and the standalone plays JSON. San Francisco completes the sweep behind Tim Lincecum and two perfect innings of relief. The Giants wasted their early chances: Willie Mays singled to open the game and was caught stealing (Pérez to Witt), and John McGraw's 2nd-inning hit and run and steal send both backfired. The breakthrough came in the 3rd off Zack Greinke: Mays singled, Will Clark doubled, Mel Ott's double scored them both, and Barry Bonds doubled Ott home for 3-0. A fourth run came in the 6th off Steve Mingori: Willie McCovey singled, Jeff Kent's hit-and-run single put him on third, and Buster Posey singled him home. Tim Lincecum takes the win: seven innings, four hits, two walks, five strikeouts, one wild pitch, and all three Kansas City runs charged to him, all at once in the 6th: Darrell Porter, pinch-hitting for Salvador Pérez, grounded out, Frank White flied out, Willie Wilson was hit by a pitch, Carlos Beltrán singled, and George Brett hit a three-run home run, the game's only homer, to make it 4-3. McGraw twice left the fatigued Lincecum in and was paid off both times: Witt struck out to end the 6th, and Lincecum worked a scoreless 7th. Zack Greinke takes the loss, charged with the three 3rd-inning runs (eight hits and one walk in 22 batters faced). Rod Beck takes the save: he entered the 9th with a one-run lead and retired Brett, Bobby Witt Jr. and John Mayberry in order. Decisions: no source prints them (the Gazette carries no win/loss/save annotations and the export prints no decisions section), so they are derived from the play log and the run charges; Beck's save follows the standard rule from his entry state (9th inning, 4-3 lead, one full inning pitched, finished the game). San Francisco's last threat went unrewarded: in the 8th Posey singled and took second on Frank White's error, the game's only error, Matt Williams was intentionally walked and Art Fletcher sacrificed both runners over, but Mays struck out. Sergio Romo pitched a perfect 8th and Beck a perfect 9th. Bob Brenly (in at catcher for Posey from the 8th) and Monte Irvin (in at left field for Bonds in the 9th) were defensive substitutes who never batted and recorded no fielding chances, so neither carries a batting or defensive line, exactly as printed. San Francisco books four RBI for four runs (Ott 2, Bonds 1, Posey 1); Kansas City books three, all Brett's. Fielding from the box score's printed fielding section: San Francisco 27 putouts and 14 assists with no double plays; Kansas City 27 putouts and 12 assists with one double play, the 4-6-3 on Ott's 9th-inning grounder (Witt to White to Mayberry), and Ott is printed with 1 GIDP. Caught stealing: Mays in the 1st, and Mike Sweeney in the 5th after his single on Yost's hit and run, a play on which the lead runner Witt was thrown out. Wild pitch: Lincecum 1 for San Francisco; no passed balls. Manager grades: McGraw graded 11 decisions (8 paid off, 3 backfired, 0 neutral), his best-graded game of the series: the top-of-the-1st steal send (Mays caught stealing, -1.11), the top-of-the-2nd hit and run (-1.11) and the top-of-the-2nd steal send (Kent held, -0.51) backfired, and everything else paid off, the top-of-the-3rd steal send best at +2.14 (Mays held on the send, then the inning produced three runs), the top-of-the-6th hit and run +0.39, the two leave-Lincecum-in calls +0.35 and +0.73, the Romo and Beck changes +0.73 each, and the Brenly and Irvin defensive substitutions +0.48 each. Yost graded 7 (3 paid off, 4 backfired): Darrell Porter's pinch hit graded +2.27, the best grade of the game (his groundout opened the three-run 6th), and the Quisenberry and Montgomery changes paid off at +0.73 each; the Mingori change backfired (-0.77, the 6th-inning run), the 5th-inning hit and run (-0.61, Witt thrown out on Sweeney's single) and steal send (Sweeney caught stealing, -0.76) backfired, and the Mayberry pinch hit backfired (-0.73). Counting checks: San Francisco plate appearances 40 equal Kansas City batters faced (Greinke 22, Mingori 6, Quisenberry 4, Montgomery 8); Kansas City plate appearances 32 equal San Francisco batters faced (Lincecum 26, Romo 3, Beck 3).
